nodes.speaker: Attendant
nodes.text: Movie-night guests hand over scarves, coats, umbrellas, and one cape with legal opinions.{pause}Then Virtue Gundam arrives, filling the coat-check doorway with several layers of armor.{pause}The attendant asks, as trained, whether the guest would like to check a coat.{pause}Virtue looks down at itself and asks which one the building considers a coat.

nodes.speaker: Attendant
nodes.text: Policy says every removable outer piece receives a separate numbered claim ticket.{pause}Virtue estimates either six pieces or forty-seven, depending on the definition of removable.{pause}The ticket machine hears this and begins making a noise associated with personal dread.{pause}Behind Virtue, the lobby line extends past the popcorn table and around a potted fern.

nodes.speaker: Virtue
nodes.text: I only need enough room to sit through a two-hour romantic comedy.{pause}The attendant measures the theater seat, then measures Virtue's shoulder armor twice.{pause}The seat is ordinary; the shoulders have opinions about neighboring postal codes.{pause}Virtue agrees to remove the outer system if every part can be returned correctly.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: A folding screen becomes an improvised changing room beside the coat-check counter.{pause}Virtue steps behind it, and the first armor panel appears over the top like sunrise.{pause}The attendant catches it, labels it LEFT SHOULDER, and places it on the nearest hook.{pause}The hook bends thoughtfully and chooses a new career as a question mark.

nodes.speaker: Attendant
nodes.text: We need a stronger rack, clearer labels, and perhaps a zoning permit.{pause}Virtue passes out the right shoulder, two leg covers, and something called a condenser block.{pause}Each piece receives a ticket; each ticket receives a backup number in pencil.{pause}The guest behind the fern asks whether the movie has already started outside.

nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.text: Layer removal reaches the point where Nadleeh stands inside the widening circle of armor.{pause}Several control cords follow, sliding across the floor with the patience of long noodles.{pause}The attendant adds CORD GROUP A to a hanger and immediately needs CORD GROUP B.{pause}Nadleeh apologizes to the line; the line applauds because the transformation looked expensive.

nodes.speaker: Nadleeh
nodes.text: Please do not knot the cords, bend the panels, reverse the shoulders, or lose ticket nine.{pause}The attendant checks the ticket roll and discovers that ticket nine printed only half a number.{pause}It could be nine, four, or a very confident lowercase letter g.{pause}They place it in a clear envelope labeled IMPORTANT MYSTERY and continue.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: A customer checks a yellow raincoat that looks harmless until it touches one control cord.{pause}Static snaps, the cord rises, and three empty hangers swing together like chimes.{pause}Nadleeh catches the cord before it can lasso the popcorn sign.{pause}The attendant gives the raincoat its own hook at a respectful diplomatic distance.

nodes.speaker: Attendant
nodes.text: We can organize this inventory by strict ticket order or by matching body position.{pause}Strict order follows policy; body position might prevent a backward shoulder later.{pause}Nadleeh says both methods sound reasonable and therefore require a binding choice.{pause}The ticket machine spits out one blank slip, apparently casting its own vote.

nodes.speaker: Nadleeh
nodes.text: The lobby clock says trailers begin in twenty minutes and the main feature in thirty.{pause}The line wants snacks, the armor wants space, and the cords want to become architecture.{pause}The attendant clears two coat racks and asks Nadleeh to choose the first organizing method.{pause}Nadleeh promises to accept any method that includes finding ticket nine again.

nodes.speaker: Attendant
nodes.text: Every panel enters a numbered lane made from rope, chairs, and two popcorn stanchions.{pause}Tickets one through eight line up beautifully; mystery nine sits between them in its envelope.{pause}Ticket ten belongs to a scarf because the machine never expected armor traffic.{pause}They rename it ten-scarf and proceed without restarting the entire lobby.

nodes.speaker: Nadleeh
nodes.text: Strict order keeps every object accountable, even when neighboring objects are unrelated.{pause}My right knee now files beside a wet umbrella, but both have excellent documentation.{pause}The attendant adds colored clips so armor, clothing, and rain gear remain separate.{pause}Mystery nine receives a gold clip, which makes it look more important than everyone.

nodes.speaker: Nadleeh
nodes.text: They outline a tiny body map on the floor using spare claim-ticket ribbon.{pause}Shoulders go north, legs south, chest pieces center, and cords curl around the edge.{pause}A customer asks whether the map is an art installation and leaves a small donation.{pause}The attendant uses the donation to buy more clips from the lobby desk.

nodes.speaker: Attendant
nodes.text: The body map makes reassembly obvious but occupies the path to theater two.{pause}Guests step carefully around the left ankle and compliment the central composition.{pause}Mystery nine fits the outline near one shoulder but could still be a chest latch.{pause}Nadleeh marks both possibilities and promises not to move suddenly during pickup.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: The claim-ticket tune returns as the coat check settles into a strange working rhythm.{pause}Whether filed by number or body map, every armor piece now has a visible home.{pause}The ordinary coats hang above them like fabric clouds over a small mechanical city.{pause}Nadleeh finally reaches the popcorn table, though one cord still follows behind.

nodes.speaker: Nadleeh
nodes.text: One medium popcorn, one small tea, and no butter within cable range, please.{pause}The vendor fills the tub, then notices the cord looped around its cardboard base.{pause}Nadleeh lifts the tub; the cord lifts a napkin dispenser and six paper straws.{pause}The attendant untangles everything with the calm focus of a person still on shift.

nodes.speaker: Attendant
nodes.text: We should coil the remaining cords before one becomes emotionally attached to the furniture.{pause}Nadleeh explains each cord has a specific bend radius and preferred return path.{pause}Together they form broad loops on the floor, securing each with paper wristbands.{pause}The loops resemble giant bows, which gives the attendant an idea for later.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: The first trailer begins behind the theater doors with a heroic burst of music.{pause}Nadleeh can hear it from the lobby but remains beside the coat check, holding a cord.{pause}The attendant offers to finish alone; Nadleeh looks at the packed inventory and stays.{pause}Missing five minutes feels better than spending the whole film worried about ticket nine.

nodes.speaker: Nadleeh
nodes.text: This is supposed to be my evening off, though I appear to have brought the whole system.{pause}The attendant says everyone brings something from work, even when it is only posture.{pause}They share popcorn beside the racks and listen to the muffled final trailer.{pause}For one quiet minute, the armor is luggage instead of an emergency.{pause}The attendant admits that the coat check feels easier with another patient person beside it.{pause}Nadleeh says being useful feels different when nobody expects a demonstration.{pause}They solve nothing during the silence, but both return to work less tightly wound.

nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.text: A rush of late guests arrives with coats, hats, and one enormous knitted blanket.{pause}The ticket machine accelerates, squeaks, and produces numbers in an increasingly nervous font.{pause}Nadleeh takes the stubs while the attendant hangs garments around the armor lanes.{pause}The line shortens because two small robots have accidentally become an excellent team.

nodes.speaker: Attendant
nodes.text: Ticket thirty-two claims a black coat, but two guests are holding ticket thirty-two.{pause}One stub is actually twenty-three viewed upside down after a butter stain.{pause}Nadleeh solves the dispute by asking each guest what was left in the pockets.{pause}Only the correct owner knows about the emergency onion cracker and gets the coat.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: The blanket is too thick for a hook and too soft to stand against the wall.{pause}Nadleeh drapes it across two lower armor panels, creating an inviting padded surface.{pause}Three waiting children sit down before anyone can declare the arrangement temporary.{pause}The panels hold perfectly, and the coat check has accidentally acquired a snack bench.

nodes.speaker: Nadleeh
nodes.text: Those panels are structural armor, not lobby furniture, though the load is acceptable.{pause}The children balance popcorn bowls on one shoulder plate and thank the tiny bench.{pause}The attendant adds a sign: SEATING PENDING OWNER APPROVAL, PLEASE DO NOT SPILL.{pause}Nadleeh changes owner approval to engineering review and leaves the sign standing.

nodes.speaker: Attendant
nodes.text: The layered march returns when intermission guests pour into the lobby all at once.{pause}Everyone wants a scarf, a coat, a restroom direction, or the rest of their popcorn.{pause}Nadleeh takes the counter while the attendant navigates the armor city behind it.{pause}Mystery nine remains untouched in its envelope, glowing with administrative importance.

nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.text: Claims move quickly until a shoulder panel is requested by someone who owns a raincoat.{pause}The attendant catches the mismatch before handing over forty kilograms of decorative defense.{pause}They return to colored clips, body position, and asking pocket questions when necessary.{pause}The main claim-ticket tune returns, calmer now that the system has learned humility.

nodes.speaker: Nadleeh
nodes.text: When the crowd clears, only six ordinary coats and all my armor remain.{pause}The romantic comedy has reached its final misunderstanding behind the closed doors.{pause}The attendant says the hero has probably failed to explain something obvious for ninety minutes.{pause}Nadleeh looks at mystery nine and says that sounds familiar.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: They open the envelope and inspect the half-printed ticket under the lobby lamp.{pause}A faint grease mark matches the hinge on the left shoulder panel, not any number.{pause}The ticket was never nine; it was a tracing made when the machine jammed.{pause}Nadleeh laughs softly, then places it with the left shoulder as an unofficial receipt.

nodes.speaker: Attendant
nodes.text: The movie ends in twelve minutes, and the coat-check line will return at full speed.{pause}We can keep the armor arranged as a snack bench for the departing crowd.{pause}Or we can lift the cords into a hanging rack with one enormous bow.{pause}Either plan must return every piece before the lobby lights shut off.

nodes.speaker: Nadleeh
nodes.text: A bench makes the heavy pieces useful and keeps every panel close to the floor.{pause}A cord rack clears the path and turns careful loops into visible organization.{pause}Nadleeh finishes the last popcorn and hears the film's audience begin to applaud.{pause}The attendant places both plans on the counter and lets the guest choose.

nodes.speaker: Attendant
nodes.text: The rush ends, and the coat-check floor appears beneath the last trail of ticket stubs.{pause}Every coat is claimed, every umbrella is dry, and no armor panel blocks the exit.{pause}The attendant counts how often guests used the counter to rest bags or retie shoes.{pause}Nadleeh counts how often a loose cord nearly caught a wheel during the busy hour.{pause}Both problems are real, even though only one solution can occupy the narrow wall.

nodes.speaker: Nadleeh
nodes.text: They test the bench plan with two helmets, a shopping bag, and the empty popcorn tub.{pause}Nothing tips, and a tired guest could sit without leaning against the numbered hooks.{pause}Then they hang three sample coats from carefully looped cords above the marked floor line.{pause}The aisle opens wide enough for a stroller and a tiny maintenance cart together.{pause}The attendant photographs both tests so tomorrow's crew can understand the choice.

nodes.speaker: Attendant
nodes.text: The bench would turn retired armor into a low, sturdy kindness for waiting guests.{pause}The cord rack would protect the busiest path and make every hanging place visible.{pause}Nadleeh checks each knot, each panel edge, and the distance to the emergency door.{pause}Neither plan treats the old equipment as clutter, which matters more than she expected.{pause}The final ticket rests between them while the lobby lights settle for the evening.

nodes.speaker: Nadleeh
nodes.text: They lock the broad panels together at knee height and spread the blanket across them.{pause}Leg armor becomes supports; shoulder pieces become armrests; a chest plate becomes the back.{pause}The earlier body map helps every part serve near its eventual reassembly position.{pause}Nadleeh tests the bench with twelve popcorn bowls and one cautious seated attendant.

nodes.speaker: Attendant
nodes.text: Departing guests rest on the bench while waiting for coats and comparing the movie.{pause}The children return the blanket, now carrying only three kernels and one heroic crease.{pause}Colored clips guide each panel from furniture duty back toward Nadleeh.{pause}The left shoulder receives its grease-mark receipt and faces the correct direction.

nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.text: Virtue reassembles without a missing panel, twisted cord, or backward shoulder.{pause}The attendant removes the final snack-bench sign and hands over one ordinary claim stub.{pause}Virtue checks its pockets and finds the emergency onion cracker from ticket thirty-two.{pause}They return it to the surprised coat owner before the lobby can create another mystery.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: Virtue leaves with every layer attached and a free pass for the next movie night.{pause}The coat check keeps a small folding bench where the armor furniture used to stand.{pause}Above it hangs the gold clip from mystery nine, labeled IMPORTANT LESSON.{pause}The attendant updates policy: unusual coats may also be useful lobby architecture.

nodes.speaker: Nadleeh
nodes.text: Nadleeh lifts the broad cord loops onto the reinforced coat racks one at a time.{pause}The loops form arches, and paper wristbands keep every bend safely within limits.{pause}Ordinary coats hang between them, indexed by color clip and gentle cable tension.{pause}The empty lobby path opens like a runway just before the theater doors swing wide.

nodes.speaker: Attendant
nodes.text: Claims flow along the cord rack from numbered section to waiting guest.{pause}Ticket order starts the search; the body map finishes every armor handoff correctly.{pause}The final yellow raincoat hangs at diplomatic distance and causes no static incident.{pause}Its owner adds one scarf to the center loop, accidentally forming a perfect bow.

nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.text: Nadleeh receives each cord in reverse order and guides it back into the armor system.{pause}The bow remains until last, framed by empty hooks and one proud ticket machine.{pause}The attendant awards it the ribbon normally given to best movie-night costume.{pause}Nadleeh wears the ribbon over the completed Virtue armor for the walk home.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: The next week, guests ask whether the famous cord bow will return for the sequel.{pause}The attendant displays a photograph beside the claim policy and reinforced rack diagram.{pause}Virtue arrives early, checks only one scarf, and finally watches every trailer.{pause}The ticket machine prints a complete nine, then rests as if its character arc is finished.
